coverage_note: 16 selected milestones, 2009–2026. Rules, formats, packs, and Arena changes; not a complete archive of releases, bans, or tournament results.

sources.title: MTG Arena State of the Formats 2026

stories.title: Mana burn is gone. Damage left the stack.
stories.summary: If your memories reach back before Magic 2010, two fundamental rules changed.
stories.before: Unused mana could cost life; combat damage used the stack.
stories.after: Unused mana normally empties each step and phase without life loss. Combat damage is assigned and dealt without a response window between them.
stories.context: You can still act before the combat damage step. Sacrificing a creature before it deals damage means it will not deal that combat damage. The 2009 article also describes an ordering rule later removed in 2024.
stories.meaning: Old combat tricks may work differently even when the cards look familiar.

stories.title: A fresh seven, every mulligan.
stories.summary: The London mulligan changed how you replace an opening hand.
stories.before: Earlier mulligan systems drew fewer cards on each attempt.
stories.after: Draw seven each time; when you keep, put one card on the bottom of your library for each non-free mulligan.
stories.context: The rollout accompanied Core Set 2020 in July 2019, with different platform dates. The old Vancouver scry step disappeared. Multiplayer games normally give a free first mulligan.
stories.meaning: You choose what to keep from a full hand before paying the card-count cost.

stories.title: Pioneer joined the format family.
stories.summary: A nonrotating format arrived with a later starting point than Modern.
stories.before: Modern reached back to sets from 2003.
stories.after: Pioneer was introduced using eligible sets from Return to Ravnica onward, with its own banned list.
stories.context: This is a dated account of the launch, not a claim that every product released since 2012 is Pioneer-legal. Its original five-card ban list is historical.
stories.meaning: A card leaving Standard does not automatically become unusable everywhere.

stories.title: Companions gained an extra step.
stories.summary: The original printed reminder text on companion cards is no longer the whole procedure.
stories.before: A companion could be cast directly from outside the game.
stories.after: Once per game, pay three generic mana at sorcery timing to put your chosen companion into your hand, then cast it normally.
stories.context: This is a special action, not an activated ability. The update applied to tabletop on June 1, Magic Online on June 3, and Arena on June 4, 2020. Deck-building requirements still apply.
stories.meaning: An old card can have updated rules without a new printing.

stories.title: Ward adds a cost to targeting.
stories.summary: Strixhaven introduced a protection ability that asks opponents to pay.
stories.before: Hexproof prevents an opponent from targeting the protected permanent.
stories.after: Ward allows targeting, but triggers to counter that opponent’s spell or ability unless they pay the ward cost.
stories.context: Ward is not an extra casting cost. It triggers after targeting; an uncounterable spell is not stopped by the countering part of ward.
stories.meaning: Targeting permission and whether a spell resolves are different questions.

stories.title: You can attack a battle you control.
stories.summary: March of the Machine introduced Battle as a card type.
stories.before: Players and planeswalkers were the familiar things to attack.
stories.after: A Siege battle’s controller chooses an opponent to protect it. Other players can attack it; damage removes defense counters.
stories.context: When its final defense counter is removed, a Siege triggers an ability that exiles it and lets its controller cast the back face without paying its mana cost. These details describe Sieges, not every possible future Battle subtype.
stories.meaning: The card’s controller and the player defending it can be different people.

stories.title: Standard expanded to three years.
stories.summary: Wizards changed the rotation model from roughly two years of sets to three.
stories.before: Older sets left Standard on a roughly two-year cycle.
stories.after: The 2023 rotation was skipped as Standard moved to a three-year model.
stories.context: This is the 2023 change. A later announcement changed the rotation calendar again, including no rotation in 2026. Set-specific exceptions and bans still matter.
stories.meaning: The Standard card pool may be larger than the one you remember.

stories.title: Play Boosters combined two pack types.
stories.summary: The change arrived with Murders at Karlov Manor in 2024.
stories.before: Draft Boosters and Set Boosters served different purposes.
stories.after: Play Boosters combined the two, keeping packs suitable for Draft and Sealed.
stories.context: Collector Boosters remained separate. Pack contents and special slots vary by release; the announcement’s exact slot breakdown describes the first implementation.
stories.meaning: The pack name changed; the set still determines the Limited environment.

stories.title: Commander’s stewardship changed.
stories.summary: The Rules Committee handed management of the format to Wizards of the Coast.
stories.before: An independent Rules Committee managed Commander.
stories.after: Wizards’ game design team took responsibility for format management.
stories.context: This milestone records the handover. Later announcements describe the Commander Format Panel and bracket system. This entry is not a complete history of Commander bans.
stories.meaning: The official place to follow format policy changed.

stories.title: Crossover booster sets entered Standard.
stories.summary: New Universes Beyond booster sets from 2025 onward joined the normal Constructed release path.
stories.before: Earlier crossover releases had different format legality.
stories.after: The new policy covers main-set cards; it does not retroactively legalize older crossovers.
stories.context: Commander products and bonus-slot cards can follow different legality rules.
stories.meaning: The franchise or pack alone does not establish legality.

stories.title: The rotation calendar moved.
stories.summary: No Standard rotation in 2026; rotation shifts to the first set of 2027.
stories.before: Rotation happened with a release later in the year.
stories.after: The announced calendar moves that reset to the start of the year from 2027.
stories.context: Standard still uses a three-year model. Consult the official set list for exceptions.
stories.meaning: A familiar autumn date no longer tells you which cards rotate.

stories.title: Double-blocking works differently.
stories.summary: Foundations removed the requirement to order blockers for combat damage.
stories.before: The attacker ordered blockers, then assigned lethal damage to earlier blockers first.
stories.after: When damage is assigned, you can divide it among blockers without that order or lethal-first requirement.
stories.context: Trample still requires lethal damage to all blockers before excess reaches the defending player or other attacked object. Combat damage still does not use the stack.
stories.meaning: An old blocking habit may give you the wrong expectation about where damage goes.

stories.title: Commander gained a shared vocabulary.
stories.summary: Five brackets were introduced to help players describe the game they want.
stories.before: Players often used informal power-level descriptions.
stories.after: The beta introduced Exhibition, Core, Upgraded, Optimized, and cEDH, alongside a Game Changers list.
stories.context: The original beta has since been revised. Use the linked current Commander reference for bracket guidance and the Game Changers list; do not treat the first announcement as today’s full rules.
stories.meaning: A bracket describes an intended experience, not a guaranteed match.

stories.title: Hybrid mana: the proposed change did not happen.
stories.summary: The February 2026 update kept the existing color-identity rule.
stories.before: A proposal would have treated hybrid colors as “either” for deck construction.
stories.after: The update retained “both”: a green/white hybrid symbol contributes both colors to color identity.
stories.context: The same update emphasized that brackets support pregame conversations rather than mechanically determining who can play together.
stories.meaning: A proposal and an adopted rule are different kinds of news.

stories.title: Arena reverted rebalanced tabletop cards.
stories.summary: The September update returned over 200 cards to their printed tabletop versions.
stories.before: Some Arena formats used adjusted versions of paper cards.
stories.after: The announced September 22 change reverted those versions and adjusted Historic and Brawl bans.
stories.context: Digital-only cards are a separate category. Consult the official banned list for current restrictions.
stories.meaning: An old Arena deck may behave differently.

stories.title: Alchemy’s retirement was announced.
stories.summary: The format is scheduled to leave Arena on February 2, 2027.
stories.before: Alchemy has its own queues and rotating card pool.
stories.after: The announced removal is upcoming, not already in effect in this edition.
stories.context: Digital-only cards remain on Arena and in other eligible formats, subject to bans or rebalancing.
stories.meaning: The format ending does not mean those cards are being deleted.

glossary.definition: A set of deck-building and play rules, including which cards are allowed. Standard, Commander, and Modern are different formats.
When older sets leave a format’s card pool. This differs from a ban on a particular card.
Whether a card is allowed in a particular format. A reprint, special slot, or product name does not settle every case.
Replacing your opening hand before play begins. Under the London procedure, you draw seven each time and bottom cards when you keep.
The game zone where spells and most activated or triggered abilities wait to resolve. Combat damage does not use it.
A card’s official current wording. Old printed text may differ; the official card database and rules settle details.
A triggered ability that counters an opponent’s targeting spell or ability unless that opponent pays the stated cost.
A card or token on the battlefield: creatures, lands, artifacts, enchantments, planeswalkers, and battles can be permanents.
Formats where you build from a restricted pool for that event. Draft involves picking cards from packs; Sealed uses opened packs.
Descriptions of intended play experiences, used with table discussion. They are not player skill rankings.
The colors that constrain a Commander deck’s card choices. Hybrid symbols normally contribute both of their colors.
An ability that can let excess combat damage pass blockers, after assigning them lethal damage.
During your main phase, with an empty stack and priority. It describes when you can act, not the action’s card type.
